LESSON: WRITING 6.5.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING: SPELLING

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.5: Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: Why are some words are commonly misspelt?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. recognise homonyms, homophones, double consonants and double vowels in written texts
2. spell commonly misspelt words for writing fluency
3. value the importance of correct spelling in written communication

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling

Teach
• Focus skill: recognise homonyms, homophones, double consonants and double vowels in written texts.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Writing 6.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why are some words are commonly misspelt?
2. Why is it important to spell words correctly?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
